fields.System.Title: PE Designer Component - Create a Milestone
fields.System.Description:
Create support for milestone creation in the Process Engine (PE) designer as part of the Designer Components feature.

Today, milestones are created through a Client Action. This is difficult to maintain because the parameters required for milestone creation are stored in the Client Action code table rather than being explicitly defined in the process itself.

This user story covers introducing milestone creation support in the PE designer so that milestone-related configuration can be modeled directly in the process definition.

The implementation is expected to include both:

  • the configuration UI in the process designer

  • the supporting XAML designer component representation needed for the process definition

The solution must also define which fields are required, optional, or conditionally available, so the designer gives clear guidance and prevents invalid or incomplete milestone setup.

Scope

The solution must support configuration of:

  • whether the Status dropdown is available

  • whether the Custom Milestone Name field is available

  • whether milestone date selection should be restricted in the future

  • whether milestone date selection should be restricted in the past

  • Dialog title = Test

  • Dialog title localization ID

  • Description

  • Description localization ID

  • Milestone Status

  • Custom Milestone Name

  • MilestoneConfigAutomationID


At minimum, the design must make it clear which values are mandatory for the process definition to be valid.

Required / Validation Expectations

The implementation must define and enforce required-field behavior for the milestone creation component.

This includes:

  • Dialog title must be required unless the design explicitly allows the dialog to rely only on localization

  • Dialog title localization ID must be required if localization-based title is supported as the configured mechanism

  • Milestone Status must be required when the status dropdown is enabled and the process requires a predefined or default milestone status

  • MilestoneConfigAutomationID must be required if milestone creation depends on linking to a configured MilestoneConfig

  • validation must prevent saving an invalid designer configuration where required milestone setup is missing

If some required rules depend on final UX or technical design decisions, the implementation must still establish explicit validation behavior and avoid leaving requiredness implicit.

Out of Scope

  • implementation of the actual end-user milestone date selection dialog itself, unless required to support the designer flow

Acceptance Criteria

  • A milestone creation option is available in the PE designer

  • Milestone creation can be configured directly in the process designer

  • Configuration is stored as part of the process definition

  • The implementation supports all listed milestone creation properties

  • Required and optional fields are explicitly defined in the designer configuration

  • The designer validates required fields and prevents invalid configuration

  • Conditional requiredness is supported where applicable

  • The solution no longer relies primarily on Client Action code table configuration for this setup

  • The implementation follows existing PE Designer Component patterns

fields.System.Title: Mailscanner migration - Register the unregistered document instead of creating a copy
fields.System.Description:
4As a system
I want to ensure the unregistered document is registered on the result IFAR case
So that I don't have multiple copies of the same document

In the current implementation of the "success" workunit, we rely on the old emailscanner code for creating IFAR cases and creating a document with the original email and attachment on the IFAR case. This means that the unregistered document created by GEMI during import will essentially become a duplicate of the request document created on the case.

The implementation should be changed in such a way that the unregistered document created by GEMI is instead registered correctly on the IFAR case. This will basically move the document from the unregistered documents archive into the IFAR case. 

If the case creation rule is set to create a case for each requested document, the original unregistered document should be registered on the first resulting case. If any further cases need to be created during processing of the request, the document registered on the first case should be referenced by the subsequent cases. This will give us the following benefits:
  1. We don't store multiple copies of the same document
  2. We can track which cases were created by the incoming request
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
When the "success" workunit has successfully created the IFAR case, the unregistered document created by GEMI is registered on the case instead of remaining in the Unregistered documents view.

If the case creation rule setting is set to create one case for each request, the unregistered document created by GEMI is registered on the first case created when processing the request. Any further cases created during processing of the request will have a reference to the registered document on the first case.

fields.System.Title: DB - Create data model for Process Model Capabilities
fields.System.Description:
The solution must support a scalable model where a Process Model can enable or disable multiple UX capabilities.

The data model should provide the foundation for configuring which capabilities are available in the case handler experience for a given Process Model.

Examples of future capabilities may include:

  • Stage Navigation

  • Milestone Timeline

  • Document Folder View

  • Task Panel

  • Checklist Panel

The model must be designed so new capabilities can be introduced without requiring major redesign.

Scope

  • Define the database/meta model for Process Model Capabilities

  • Define how capabilities are related to a Process Model

  • Support storing enabled/disabled capabilities per Process Model

  • Ensure the model is extensible for future capability types

  • Provide a stable foundation for admin UI and runtime UI integration

Acceptance Criteria

  • A Process Model can store one or more configured capabilities

  • Each capability can be enabled or disabled per Process Model

  • The data model supports adding new capability types in the future

  • The model is suitable for use by both Process Model Admin and case handler UI

  • The implementation replaces the need for a single dedicated property for one specific view

fields.System.Title: Stage defined process - NOR "Mottak" - ENU "Received- Process"
fields.System.Description:
As a process owner, I want to be to have a repeatable block that can be uses for assessing an application in receiveing phase, so that I can process the application effeciently

Details:

1. Component Identity

Proposed Name: Received Process (NO: Mottak)
Originating Process: N/A
Author: MJ
Date:

One-Sentence Description:
Registers initial milestones on the case and checks for major deficiencies

2. Business Intent

Describe the business situation where this building block is used.

  • Trigger event: 
  • Intended outcome: Outbound document created and dispatched.
  • primary actors involved: Case worker

Do not describe implementation steps. Describe purpose.

3. Functional Behavior (Explicit Sequence Required)

Describe the expected flow in ordered steps.

For each step, use the following structure:

Step 1 – Set Application Received

  • Purpose: Set milestone date for application received
  • Arguments / Parameters:
    • Milestone type —hardcoded - Application received
    • Application received
  • Mandatory or Optional: Mandatory
  • Client action, server action or other: Client action
  • Completion condition: Milestone Updated

Step 2 – Set Application Complete

  • Purpose: Set milestone date for application complete
  • Arguments / Parameters:
    • Milestone type —hardcoded - Application received
    • Application received
  • Mandatory or Optional: Mandatory
  • Client action, server action or other: Client action
  • Completion condition: Milestone Updated

Step 3 – Major deficiency

  • Purpose: Register that there is a major deficiency on the case and create a sub-process the deficiency
  • Arguments / Parameters:
    • CaseId - inherited from case
    • Automation : ID of the workunit to be invoked from the server action.
  • Mandatory or Optional: Mandatory
  • Client action, server action or other: server action
  • Completion condition: When executed, the server action invokes the major deficiency process and inserts this as a sub-process under this current process
  • (invoke oneliner for attatching process)


Step 5 – Create meeting invitation/Appointment in calendar
  • Purpose
    • As a process manager I should be able to configure -Create meeting invitation activity with a title and selection of participanso that the case manager can easily create a meeting invitation based on contacts in the process and the meeting is automatically added to the Outlook calendar.
    • As a case manager I should be able to create a meeting invitation with a predefined title, select participants from the case, and specify the meeting date so that the meeting invitation is automatically created in my Outlook calendar.

  • Arguments / Parameters:
    • Meeting title: Configurable
    • Participant role: Case roles from code table:  Contact-Case role
  • Mandatory or Optional: Optional
  • Client action, server action or other: client action (create appointment)
  • Completion condition: Meeting created



Step 5 – Send task/notice to department / case manager
  • Purpose: Send task/notice to department / case manager
  • Arguments / Parameters:
    • CaseId - inherited from case

  • Mandatory or Optional: Mandatory
  • Client action, server action or other: client action
  • Completion condition:  notice creates



6. Dependencies

  • Requires Business Rules Engine? (Yes/No) No
  • Requires external integration? No
  • Synchronous / asynchronous? Synchrnous

High-level only.

Submission Outcome (Product Use Only):
☐ Approved for Design
☐ Needs Refinement
☐ Rejected (Insufficient Abstraction / Reuse Case)















The document describes a standardized reception process for processing applications and inquiries , with a focus on configurable activities, milestones and administration through a system. The process ensures traceability, automation and flexibility in case processing.
Standard activities in the process
1. Application received
(dialog "Register date of application received" creates milestone set in admin)
2. Application is complete
(dialog "Register date of complete application" creates milestone set in admin)
3. Application has a significant deficiency
(starts subprocess "Deficiency letter - Significant deficiency" outgoing document)
4. Write letter
(outgoing letter with approval)
5. Send task/notice to department / case manager
(dialog to add note, deadline and recipient)
6. Create meeting request
(creates new appointment in Outlook)
Additional:
• Automatic receipt confirmation without caseworker involvement
• Automatic status change when transitioning between activities
• Automatic start/stop of internal and external time based on activity/milestone

Details:
  1. Registration of receipt and complete application: The system allows registration of the date of receipt and the date of complete application via dialogs that automatically create completed milestones. Acknowledgement letters are sent automatically when registering receipt. 
  2. Configuration in administration: The process manager can configure dialog titles, date fields, milestones, visibility and time calculation for activities, which can be reused across processes. Changes only apply to new cases. 
  3. Deficiency letters and document production: In the event of deficiencies, a sub-process for outgoing letters is started with predefined templates, roles, paragraph selection and approval routines. Milestones are set automatically upon completion, and the case processing time can be paused. 
  4. Task and notification: Tasks can be created for departments or case managers with notes, deadlines and recipients. Tasks can be blocking and notify when due. Completion can automatically move the case further in the process. 
  5. Meeting invitation: Activities to create meeting invitations in Outlook can be configured with title and participants from the case. Case managers can select the date and participants, and the invitation is automatically added to the calendar. 
  6. Link to external systems: Activities can open pre-configured links to external systems or websites, with logging of who and when the link is opened. Opening can be linked to milestones for traceability. 
  7. General activity rules: All activities can be activated/deactivated per case type, linked to milestones, affect time calculation, be visible or hidden, and configured with blocking and manual override. Changes only apply to new cases. 
  8. Time and milestone management: Activities can be set to start or stop internal or external time, and milestones are automatically created at relevant events to ensure correct case flow and time tracking

fields.System.Title: Started - PM - Performance - Identify instance-specific fields in cloned ProcessModel sub-entities
fields.System.Description:
When a case is created, the system clones the entire ProcessModelConfig hierarchy ( StageConfigs, StageProcessConfigs, MilestoneConfigs,).

This US focuses exclusively on determining which cloned sub-entities actually contain instance-specific data that justifies cloning.

We need a complete technical overview of whether MilestoneConfigs (MILCs), StageConfigs (STACs), and StageProcessConfigs (STAPCs) contain fields that differ between the cloned case-specific model and the original ProcessModelConfig.

The goal is to identify whether cloning is technically required for these entities, based solely on whether they store instance-level state during case execution.

This analysis is needed to validate whether excessive data growth (e.g., databases with millions of MilestoneConfigs) is needed or if we can start thinking differently


Purpose:

To build a factual foundation so we know:

  • Which ProcessModel sub-entities truly contain per-case state, and

  • Which ones might be cloned unnecessarily, causing massive data growth and slow queries.
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
• For each entity type below, list all fields and classify them as:

    • Configuration field (same across all cases)

    • Instance-specific field (changes per case)

    • Potentially instance-specific (usage unclear, requires deeper review)

  • Entities to include:

    • milc_milestoneconfig

    • stac_stageconfig

    • stapc_stageprocessconf

    • Any child tables directly tied to these (Connection tables)

  • For each entity type:

    • Compare instance rows with their template/PMC source rows

    • Identify fields whose values differ after cloning

    • Identify fields that are modified during case lifetime

  • Determine whether cloned rows actually store per-case state (e.g., IsInitialized flags, calculated dates, dynamic metadata)

  • Identify any cloned entities where:

    • Fields never change across cases, or

    • Values always match the PMC source → potential unnecessary data duplication

  • Deliver a short summary describing:

    • Which entities appear to truly require cloning

    • Which entities appear to be static and might not need to be cloned

    • Any anomalies explaining massive MILC growth

fields.System.Title: PM - Performance – Investigate abnormal MilestoneConfig & StageProcessConfig row counts
fields.System.Description:
Some customer databases contain extremely high numbers of MilestoneConfigs (MILC) and StageProcessConfigs (STAPC).
Before we can optimize performance or adjust logic, we must determine whether these volumes are legitimate outcomes of normal case creation, or if they indicate unintended duplication or repeated cloning.

This User Story is strictly about establishing whether the current data growth is expected or not.
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
• Determine how many MILC/STAPC rows are created per case.

  • Verify whether these numbers align with expected behavior.

  • Identify whether the volumes appear:

    • legitimate (normal system behavior), or

    • unexpected (potential bug or unintended duplication).

  • Deliver a short conclusion stating one of the two:

    • “Data volume appears valid”, or

    • “Data volume appears invalid — requires further investigation.”

fields.System.Title: PM - Performance – Analyse of legacy StageTemplate behaviour and requirements for redesign - UseLatestVersion
fields.System.Description:
The historical StageTemplate model allowed a StageConfig to belong to a ProcessModel/ProcessModelConfig while referencing a template via ToTemplate, optionally combined with UseLatestTemplateVersion.

This resulted in three types of StageConfigs:

  1. Custom Stage (no template reference)

  2. StageTemplate instance not using latest version

  3. StageTemplate instance using latest version

In the new admin interface, this model has been simplified:
When creating a StageConfig, the user must explicitly choose:

  • Custom Stage

  • Copy of Template

  • Template

Choosing “Copy of Template” now creates a direct copy without ToTemplate.
Choosing “Template” now always implies UseLatestVersion = true.
This makes the old UseLatestTemplateVersion behavior obsolete.

However, before we redesign the logic and clean up old data, we must verify that legacy template-copies indeed have their own MilestoneConfigs (MILCs) and StageProcessConfigs (STPCs).
If not, cleanup or migration could break customer data.

This User Story focuses solely on analysing legacy StageTemplate use and understanding the real data patterns.

Purpose:

To ensure that the legacy StageTemplate design is fully understood before removing UseLatestTemplateVersion and converting old template-copies into the new, simplified model.
This analysis ensures that the redesign will not break existing customer data or introduce regressions.
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
Acceptance Criteria

  • Identify all StageConfigs in existing databases that:

    • have ToTemplate > 0

    • and UseLatestTemplateVersion = 0

  • For each such StageConfig, determine whether it has its own:

    • MilestoneConfigs (MILC)

    • StageProcessConfigs (STPC)

  • Document whether these legacy “template copies” behave as:

    • True copies (isolated, with their own sub-entities), or

    • Partial/incomplete copies that still depend on template structures.

  • Validate whether any PMC currently relies on the old UseLatestTemplateVersion behavior.

  • Produce a clear summary indicating:

    • Whether UseLatestTemplateVersion can safely be removed

    • Which StageConfigs require migration or conversion to “copy mode”

    • Any edge cases or data inconsistencies discovered

fields.System.Title: PM360 - Urestricted Milestones - Add Milestones on a Closed Stage
fields.System.Description:
As a caseworker
I want to be able to add missing milestones to a stage that has already been closed
So that all relevant events in the case handling process are registered and contribute to correct statistics, internal reporting, and KOSTRA output.

In the current solution, stages that have been closed cannot receive new milestones. If a milestone was forgotten, misinterpreted, or documented late, the caseworker has no way to add it after the stage is completed. This results in incomplete event history, inaccurate reporting, and manual workarounds outside the system.

This user story introduces the ability to add new milestones to closed stages in a controlled, safe, and fully traceable manner. Adding milestones must not reopen the stage or alter its process state but must allow correct documentation of events that should have been recorded earlier.

Requirements

It must be possible to open a milestone creation dialog for a closed stage and register a new milestone.

The standard validation rules for milestones must still apply:

  • Status rules (Planned / Reached / Cancelled)

  • Concurrency rules

  • Valid combinations of type + status

  • Date validation

Adding a milestone must not:

  • Reopen the stage

  • Change stage status

  • Regenerate processes or content under the stage

A message must inform the user that the stage remains closed and the milestone is being added solely for documentation and reporting accuracy.

 “This stage is closed. You may adjust milestone information for documentation and reporting purposes only. The stage will remain closed, and no workflow or processes will be triggered.”
Ensure this message it displayed to user when editing or adding a milestone opn a closed stage



Non-Goals

Reopening closed stages

  • Adding or modifying processes or tasks on closed stages

  • Structural changes to the stage or the Process Model
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
AC1 – User can open milestone creation dialog on a closed stage

Given a stage is in status Closed or Terminated
When the caseworker selects “Add Milestone” on that stage
Then the system must open the standard milestone creation dialog

AC2 – Standard milestone validation rules apply

Given the user is adding a new milestone to a closed stage
When the milestone type, status, or date is selected
Then all standard milestone validations must run, including:

  • Allowed milestone statuses

  • Concurrency rules, if changing to a type that already exist

  • Valid type/status combinations

  • Required milestone types

  • Date validation rules

AC2 – User receives context information

Given the milestone creation & edit dialog is open for a closed stage
When the user views the dialog the following text should be displayed : 
“This stage is closed. You may adjust milestone information for documentation and reporting purposes only. The stage will remain closed, and no workflow or processes will be triggered.”

fields.System.Title: PM - P360 - UI - Analyze all API calls executed during case UI load
fields.System.Description:
When opening a case, the UI triggers multiple API calls to load Process Model data and lookup lists. Several of these calls may fetch information that is not immediately needed, such as lists only used when opening dialogs (e.g., “Available Milestones”, “Available Stages”, “Available Processes”).

We need a complete analysis of all API calls executed during case UI initialization to identify:

  • Which calls are essential for initial rendering.

  • Which calls are unused until a later user action.

  • Which data sets can be lazily loaded, cached, batched, or removed.

  • Whether duplicated or overlapping calls occur.

  • How much each call contributes to overall load time.

The analysis must create a clear overview that allows us to decide what can be optimized in follow-up stories.

fields.System.Title: PM - Performance – Analyze - Could we wait with creating the instances of the stac/milc/stapc until instantiation and get those from the templates
fields.System.Description:
Currently we are creating ALL stac, milc, stapc when instantiating a new case. Do we need to do that?

Could we wait with creating the non-autogenerate configs, until they are actually needed.

This would mean that all drop downs for "create new ###" should get the values from the "template" on the PMC

When instantiating a new stage/milestone/process it should be checked: Do we have the correct config on the instance, or else create it.


The meta insert handlers should take care of copying the configs from the PMC to the instance if needed.

fields.System.Title: Stage Closure Blocked Message Is Misleading When Milestones Are Still Active
fields.System.Description:
Summary

When a stage contains active milestones or  documents but its processes are terminated or removed, attempting to close the stage is blocked as expected.
However, the message shown to the user is currently presented as an error, which is misleading.

This is not a system failure — it is expected workflow behavior — but the UX communicates it incorrectly.

Reproduction Steps

  1. Create a case with a Process Model (PM)

  2. Navigate to a stage

  3. Terminate or remove all processes under the stage

  4. Leave milestones active on the stage

  5. Attempt to change the stage status to Closed

  6. Observe the system message

Actual Result

A generic or technical error message is displayed to the user, implying that something is broken or failed.


Expected Result

The system should display a user-guiding informational message, explaining why the stage cannot yet be closed and what needs to be done.

This is a workflow constraint, not an error.


Screenshot for issue in master: 



ℹ️ Why this is not an error

  1. This is a workflow rule  A stage can only be closed when all required items (processes, documents, milestones) are completed. 
  2. The system is enforcing that rule correctly  Nothing is broken and the user didn’t do anything wrong. 
  3. The message explains what’s blocking the action  It tells the user why closing the stage is not allowed yet and what needs to be completed. 
Summary: Errors mean something failed. This is a workflow rule blocking an action until requirements are met.

ℹ️ The important distinction

  1. Technically, the action fails  From the system’s point of view, closing the stage returns an error because conditions aren’t met. 
  2. Functionally, this is expected behavior  The system is designed to block the action in this situation. 
  3. UX should reflect user intent, not system internals  Users should see this as “you can’t do this yet,” not “something went wrong.”

I’m proposing two solutions. The first one should be the preferred approach.


  1. ✅ Preferred Solution: Alert Message Instead of an Error

Replace the error with a blocking alert  message that clearly explains:

  • Why the action is blocked

  • What needs to be completed

  • That this is expected behavior


Alert message : 


2. Alternative Solution.


Popup message:

https://www.figma.com/design/xDdBz4zFW3l13ZBEqUleeF/Process-Models?node-id=295-3184&t=zIE8fxJQuUNNNzeJ-1

fields.System.Title: IFAR processing should exclude file references
fields.System.Description:
As a user
I want to not include file references when processing IFAR cases
In order to avoid potential issues with security classification of referenced files

Feature toggle: IfarExcludeFileReferences
In the current implementation, file references are excluded from the request section of IFAR cases, but included in the response document template. This causes a lot of confusion making it difficult to actually determine if the correct files are included. Furthermore we risk disclosing sensitive material since the referenced files can come from any document with any classification.

In order to avoid these issues, we need to make the following changes:

When adding requests: 
  • An icon should warn the user that a document has files references (similar to notifying the user that a document is not finalized). When hovering over the icon, the following text should be presented: "This document references file(s) on another document. To include the file(s) please add the original document to your access request case". 
  • The icon "error_icon.svg" could be used (follow-up w. designer).


When the document is actually being added:
  • File references should not be included. 
    • The same icon as mentioned above should be displayed for the document
  • If a document contains only references, no request activity should be created for that document.


When generating the response document:
  • Ensure file references are not added to the response document.

When generating the response template:
  • Ensure file references are not included in the template
  • Ensure that the file count on the document is presented correctly (without file references). 
    • This might require a new META field

fields.System.Title: IFAR - Redaction - Enable flattening for PDF forms and emails
fields.System.Description:
As a user
I want to have reliable redaction of PDF forms and email
So that I can safely transmit redacted files to the requester

Currently when redacting PDF forms, the redactions are not complete. In the resulting PDFs, sometimes text underneath redaction blocks can be copied and thus viewed. This has to be prevented in order to ensure our customers don't accidentally leak classified information.
fields.Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria:
General note: The easiest way to spot if a file has been flattened is to zoom the redacted file as much as possible in an external viewer (download the file from 360 and open in either browser or dedicated application like Acrobat Reader). If the file content (especially text) appears pixelated, then the file has been flattened. The time spent on processing is also an indicator - flattening takes longer than just burning the redactions.

When the feature toggle "FileViewerRedactionTiffMode" is OFF:
  • Redactions happen normally, and PDF forms and emails (MSG and EML) sometimes leak information. The burned PDFs have not been flattened (converted to TIFF and back into PDF)
When the feature toggle "FileViewerRedactionTiffMode" is ON:
  • If the file is a PDF with form fields OR the file is either EML or MSG, the flattening process will run before the redactions are burned. Other file types are not run through the flattening process.
  • For testing the difference in behavior with PDFs, use the files attached to this user story.

fields.System.Title: UX - Design Process Model Capabilities Configuration UI

Design the user interface for configuring Process Model Capabilities in Process Model Administration.

The Capabilities configuration allows administrators to enable or disable specific user experience capabilities that will be available to case handlers when a Process Model is used.

The UI should allow administrators to easily understand which capabilities are available and configure them per Process Model in a clear and scalable way.

This design will serve as the foundation for enabling or disabling UX functionality in the case handler interface based on Process Model configuration.

Goals

Create a clear and intuitive interface for configuring UX capabilities per Process Model.

Ensure the design supports:

  • Multiple capabilities

  • Future capabilities being added

  • Easy understanding of what each capability does

  • Consistent integration with the existing Process Model Administration UI.

Scope

The design should include:

Capabilities configuration section

A new configuration section in Process Model Admin where capabilities can be managed.

Capability listing

A list of available capabilities with:

  • name

  • description

  • enabled/disabled state

Example capabilities may include:

  • Stage Navigation

  • Milestone Timeline

  • Document Folder View

  • Task Panel

  • Checklist Panel

Enable / disable mechanism

Capabilities should be configurable using a clear UI mechanism such as:

  • toggle switches

  • checkboxes

  • or similar patterns consistent with existing admin UI.

Help / explanation

Each capability should include a short description explaining what it enables in the case handler interface.

fields.System.Title: PE Designer Component - Create a Milestone Dialog in Case Handling view
fields.System.Description:
Create the runtime milestone creation dialog in the Case Handling UI.

This user story covers the end-user dialog shown in the case handler interface when a process action triggers milestone creation. The dialog must render and behave based on the milestone creation configuration defined in the Process Engine process definition.

The dialog is not part of the PE designer itself. It is the runtime UI that acts on the configured milestone creation element and allows the case handler to provide the necessary values when creating a milestone.

The implementation must support rendering configured fields, applying visibility rules, enforcing required fields, and validating milestone date restrictions.

Scope

The Case Handling UI must support a milestone creation dialog that can render the following configured elements:

  • Dialog title

  • Dialog title localization ID

  • Description

  • Description localization ID

  • Status dropdown, when enabled

  • Custom Milestone Name field, when enabled

  • Milestone date input

  • Validation for restricting milestone date selection in the future

  • Validation for restricting milestone date selection in the past

The dialog must use the configured values from the process definition and behave consistently with the milestone creation setup defined in the PE designer.

Functional Requirements

  • The dialog must open from the configured milestone creation action in the case handler flow

  • The dialog must display title and description based on configuration

  • Localization IDs must be supported where configured

  • The Status field must be shown only when enabled in configuration

  • The Custom Milestone Name field must be shown only when enabled in configuration

  • Required fields must be clearly indicated in the UI

  • The dialog must validate required input before submission

  • The dialog must prevent invalid milestone date selection based on configured past/future restrictions

  • The dialog must submit the entered values in a format that can be used for milestone creation

Out of Scope

  • PE designer configuration UI

  • XAML designer component implementation

  • Definition of milestone creation metadata in the process definition

  • Backend creation logic, unless minor adjustments are required to support the dialog contract

Acceptance Criteria

  • A milestone creation dialog is available in the Case Handling UI

  • The dialog renders based on milestone creation configuration from the process definition

  • Configured title and description are shown correctly

  • Localization-based title and description are supported

fields.System.Title: Move CreateMilestoneOnStage logic to MilestoneMetaHandlers
fields.System.Description:
As a

developer and maintainer of the Process Platform and SIF (interaction framework)

I want

the CreateMilestoneOnStage logic moved from MilestoneManager into the Milestone Meta handlers (MilestoneMetaInsert and related handlers)

So that

all milestone creation goes through the same automation and business logic, regardless of whether it is triggered via direct MilestoneManager calls or via SIF/Meta execution.

Background

Today there are two different paths for creating milestones on a stage:

  1. Direct path: Callers (ProcessEngine activities, MilestoneHandler, eByggesak operations, etc.) call MilestoneManager.CreateMilestoneOnStage(), which contains the full logic (validation, status computation, parameter building, etc.).
  2. SIF/Meta path: SIF uses Meta handlers. When SIF creates milestones, it executes Meta statements that are handled by MilestoneMetaInsert and related handlers. MilestoneManager is not used.

Because of this split, SIF and direct callers can end up with different automation and business rules for milestone creation.

Acceptance criteria

  • AllCreateMilestoneOnStage logic (validation, status computation, parameter building, date handling, etc.) is implemented in the Milestone Meta handlers (e.g.MilestoneMetaInsert or shared base classes).
  • MilestoneManager.CreateMilestoneOnStagedelegates to the Meta execution path (e.g. by building and executing the appropriate Meta statement) instead of containing its own logic.
  • SIF and direct callers use the same logic when creating milestones on a stage.
  • Existing unit and integration tests forCreateMilestoneOnStagecontinue to pass.
  • No regression in behavior for ProcessEngine activities,MilestoneHandler, eByggesak, and other current callers.

Technical notes

  • Current callers of MilestoneManager.CreateMilestoneOnStage: CreateMilestone (ProcessEngine), MilestoneHandler, eByggesak CreateMilestoneOnStageOperation, MilestoneGenerator, MilestoneMetaHandler (eByggesak), SetWinterBreak job, etc.
  • Target: Logic should live in MilestoneMetaInsert (or shared MilestoneMetaHandler base) so that both direct calls and SIF Meta execution use the same rules.
  • Design: MilestoneManager.CreateMilestoneOnStage can become a thin wrapper that builds a Milestone INSERT statement and executes it via Meta, ensuring all creation flows through the Meta handlers.

fields.System.Title: Support Stage pre-selection in New Document Wizard and Dialog when opened from Process Engine client action
fields.System.Description:
Description:
When a user opens the New Document Wizard or New Document Dialog from a Process Engine client action (NewDocumentWizard, NewDocumentDialog), the backend will pass a Stage (or StageId) URL parameter. The BIF views must read this parameter and pre-select the stage in the document creation form so that the new document is linked to the correct stage (Document.ToStage).

Context:
- Process Engine client actions generate URLs to locator/DMS/Document/New/{archive} (wizard) and locator/DMS/Document/New/Dialog (dialog)
- Backend will add Stage={stageRecno} to the query string when the designer has configured a stage (via NewDocumentStageId bound to GetCurrentStageId.Result)
- Document entity has ToStage field – the BIF must set this when the Stage parameter is present

Relevant BIF files (to investigate):
- core-BIFStore/BIFStore/standard/User Interface/Document/JournalDocumentInsertWizardView.*.bxml
- New Document Dialog view (locator DMS.Document.New.Dialog)
- Document entity uses DocumentEntityData.ToStage; StageConfigComboControl filters by stage

Acceptance Criteria:
- When the New Document Wizard is opened with Stage (or StageId) in the URL, the stage dropdown/selector is pre-selected with the given stage recno
- When the New Document Dialog is opened with Stage (or StageId) in the URL, the stage is pre-selected
- The created document has ToStage set to the pre-selected stage
- When no Stage parameter is present, behavior is unchanged (no regression)

Technical Notes:
- URL parameter name: confirm with backend – likely Stage or StageId (integer, stage recno)
- BIF uses [CONTEXT(paramName,Primary,true)] for URL parameters
- Document insert wizard has StageConfigComboControl and DocumentEntityData.ToStage
- Verify whether StageConfigComboControl expects stage recno or stage config recno
